sanskrit: sahasram ekaṃ varṣāṇāṃ tataḥ kaliyugaṃ smṛtam tasya varṣaśataṃ saṃdhyā saṃdhyāṃśaś ca tataḥ param saṃdhyāsaṃdhyāṃśayos tulyaṃ pramāṇam upadhāraya
english: One thousand years is declared the Kali age; its twilight is one hundred years, and after that the twilight-fraction likewise — understand that the twilight and the twilight-fraction are equal in measure.

sanskrit: kṣīṇe kaliyuge caiva pravartati kṛtaṃ yugam eṣā dvādaśasāhasrī yugākhyā parikīrtitā
english: When the Kali age has expired, the Kṛta age commences again. This cycle of twelve thousand years is celebrated as the span of a yuga.

sanskrit: etat sahasraparyantam aho brāhmam udāhṛtam viśvaṃ hi brahmabhavane sarvaśaḥ parivartate lokānāṃ manujavyāghra pralayaṃ taṃ vidur budhāḥ
english: A thousand such cycles constitute what is called one day of Brahmā. The entire universe revolves continuously within Brahmā's abode, O tiger among men; the wise call that the dissolution of the worlds.

sanskrit: alpāvaśiṣṭe tu tadā yugānte bharatarṣabha sahasrānte narāḥ sarve prāyaśo 'nṛtavādinaḥ
english: When little remains of the age, O bull of the Bhāratas, at the end of the thousand-year cycle, almost all men become speakers of falsehood.

sanskrit: yajñapratinidhiḥ pārtha dānapratinidhis tathā vratapratinidhiś caiva tasmin kāle pravartate
english: In that era, O Pārtha, substitutes for sacrifice, substitutes for giving, and substitutes for vows prevail everywhere.

sanskrit: brāhmaṇāḥ śūdrakarmāṇas tathā śūdrā dhanārjakāḥ kṣatradharmeṇa vāpy atra vartayanti gate yuge
english: Brahmins perform the duties of śūdras; śūdras pursue wealth-earning; and some maintain themselves by the law of warriors — such is the state when the age has passed.

sanskrit: nivṛttayajñasvādhyāyāḥ piṇḍodakavivarjitāḥ brāhmaṇāḥ sarvabhakṣāś ca bhaviṣyanti kalau yuge
english: In the Kali age brahmins will abandon sacrifice and Vedic recitation, will neglect the offerings of food and water to ancestors, and will eat everything indiscriminately.

sanskrit: ajapā brāhmaṇās tāta śūdrā japaparāyaṇāḥ viparīte tadā loke pūrvarūpaṃ kṣayasya tat
english: Brahmins will cease to recite mantras, dear one, while śūdras will be devoted to repetition of prayers. When the world is thus inverted, that is the first sign of the final dissolution.

sanskrit: bahavo mleccharājānaḥ pṛthivyāṃ manujādhipa mithyānuśāsinaḥ pāpā mṛṣāvādaparāyaṇāḥ
english: Many mleccha kings will rule the earth, O lord of men — sinful rulers who govern unjustly and are wholly devoted to falsehood.

sanskrit: āndhrāḥ śakāḥ pulindāś ca yavanāś ca narādhipāḥ kāmbojā aurṇikāḥ śūdrās tathābhīrā narottama
english: Āndhra kings, Śakas, Pulindas, Yavanas, Kāmbojas, Aurṇikas, śūdras, and Ābhīras, O best of men — all will rule as lords of the earth.

sanskrit: na tadā brāhmaṇaḥ kaś cit svadharmam upajīvati kṣatriyā api vaiśyāś ca vikarmasthā narādhipa
english: Then no brahmin will live by his own dharma, and kṣatriyas and vaiśyas too will be established in wrong livelihood, O lord of men.

sanskrit: alpāyuṣaḥ svalpabalā alpatejaḥparākramāḥ alpadehālpasārāś ca tathā satyālpabhāṣiṇaḥ
english: Men will be short-lived, of little strength, of scant energy and valour, of puny body and little substance, and sparing in speaking the truth.

sanskrit: bahuśūnyā janapadā mṛgavyālāvṛtā diśaḥ yugānte samanuprāpte vṛthā ca brahmacāriṇaḥ bhovādinas tathā śūdrā brāhmaṇāś cāryavādinaḥ
english: When the end of the age arrives, districts will be largely deserted, the regions will be overrun by deer and beasts of prey, the celibate students will be false, śūdras will use the honorific 'bho,' and brahmins will address each other as 'ārya.'

sanskrit: yugānte manujavyāghra bhavanti bahujantavaḥ na tathā ghrāṇayuktāś ca sarvagandhā viśāṃ pate rasāś ca manujavyāghra na tathā svāduyoginaḥ
english: At the end of the age, O tiger among men, many creatures will be born, yet the sense of smell will not register all fragrances as before, O lord of the people, and tastes too will not yield their former sweetness, O tiger among men.

sanskrit: bahuprajā hrasvadehāḥ śīlācāravivarjitāḥ mukhebhagāḥ striyo rājan bhaviṣyanti yugakṣaye
english: Women will be prolific but small in body, devoid of virtue and good conduct, and bold of face and tongue, O king — such will they be at the decline of the age.

sanskrit: aṭṭaśūlā janapadā śivaśūlāś catuṣpathāḥ keśaśūlāḥ striyo rājan bhaviṣyanti yugakṣaye
english: Districts will be marked by watchtower-stakes, crossroads by jackal-stakes, and women by the stake of their hair, O king — so it will be at the decline of the age.

sanskrit: alpakṣīrās tathā gāvo bhaviṣyanti janādhipa alpapuṣpaphalāś cāpi pādapā bahuvāyasāḥ
english: Cows will give little milk, O lord of the people, trees will bear few flowers and fruits, and crows will abound.

sanskrit: brahmavadhyāvaliptānāṃ tathā mithyābhiśaṃsinām nṛpāṇāṃ pṛthivīpāla pratigṛhṇanti vai dvijāḥ
english: Twice-born men will accept gifts from kings who are tainted with the murder of brahmins and who are false accusers, O guardian of the earth.

sanskrit: lobhamohaparītāś ca mithyādharmadhvajāvṛtāḥ bhikṣārthaṃ pṛthivīpāla cañcūryante dvijair diśaḥ
english: Overcome by greed and delusion, wrapped in the banner of false dharma, the twice-born will wander the directions in search of alms, O guardian of the earth.

sanskrit: karabhārabhayāt puṃso gṛhasthāḥ parimoṣakāḥ municchadmākṛticchannā vāṇijyam upajīvate
english: Householders, fearing the burden of taxes, will become plunderers; disguised under the pretence of ascetics' garb, they will make their living by trade.

sanskrit: mithyā ca nakharomāṇi dhārayanti narās tadā arthalobhān naravyāghra vṛthā ca brahmacāriṇaḥ
english: Men will falsely wear long nails and body hair out of greed for wealth, O tiger among men, and celibate students will live in vain observance.

sanskrit: āśrameṣu vṛthācārāḥ pānapā gurutalpagāḥ aihalaukikam īhante māṃsaśoṇitavardhanam
english: Those in the hermitages will be of worthless conduct — drunkards, violators of their teacher's bed — and they will seek only worldly gain, the fattening of flesh and blood.

sanskrit: bahupāṣaṇḍasaṃkīrṇāḥ parānnaguṇavādinaḥ āśramā manujavyāghra na bhavanti yugakṣaye
english: At the decline of the age, O tiger among men, hermitages will be crowded with many heretics who praise the food of others — true hermitages will not exist.

sanskrit: yathartuvarṣī bhagavān na tathā pākaśāsanaḥ na tadā sarvabījāni samyag rohanti bhārata adharmaphalam atyarthaṃ tadā bhavati cānagha
english: The glorious Indra will not rain seasonably then, O Bhārata; all seeds will not sprout properly; and the fruit of unrighteousness will be exceedingly great in that time, O sinless one.

sanskrit: tathā ca pṛthivīpāla yo bhaved dharmasaṃyutaḥ alpāyuḥ sa hi mantavyo na hi dharmo 'sti kaś cana
english: And in that time, O guardian of the earth, whoever is endowed with dharma is to be considered short-lived — there is no dharma of any kind that avails.

sanskrit: bhūyiṣṭhaṃ kūṭamānaiś ca paṇyaṃ vikrīṇate janāḥ vaṇijaś ca naravyāghra bahumāyā bhavanty uta
english: People will sell goods mostly by false weights and measures, and merchants, O tiger among men, will be full of deceit.

sanskrit: dharmiṣṭhāḥ parihīyante pāpīyān vardhate janaḥ dharmasya balahāniḥ syād adharmaś ca balī tathā
english: The righteous will decline and the sinful will increase; dharma will lose its strength while adharma will wax powerful.

sanskrit: alpāyuṣo daridrāś ca dharmiṣṭhā mānavās tadā dīrghāyuṣaḥ samṛddhāś ca vidharmāṇo yugakṣaye
english: In the decline of the age, those humans who are most righteous will be short-lived and poor, while those who are lawless will be long-lived and prosperous.

sanskrit: adharmiṣṭhair upāyaiś ca prajā vyavaharanty uta saṃcayenāpi cālpena bhavanty āḍhyā madānvitāḥ
english: People will deal by means of unrighteous stratagems, and even with a small hoard they become wealthy and arrogant.

sanskrit: dhanaṃ viśvāsato nyastaṃ mitho bhūyiṣṭhaśo narāḥ hartuṃ vyavasitā rājan māyācārasamanvitāḥ
english: Men, acting with trickery, will for the most part be determined to steal wealth that has been entrusted to them by others in good faith, O king.

sanskrit: puruṣādāni sattvāni pakṣiṇo 'tha mṛgās tathā nagarāṇāṃ vihāreṣu caityeṣv api ca śerate
english: Man-eating creatures, birds and beasts alike, will take their rest in the pleasure-gardens and sacred-tree shrines of cities.

sanskrit: saptavarṣāṣṭavarṣāś ca striyo garbhadharā nṛpa daśadvādaśavarṣāṇāṃ puṃsāṃ putraḥ prajāyate
english: Women of seven or eight years will bear children, O king, and men of ten or twelve years will beget sons.

sanskrit: bhavanti ṣoḍaśe varṣe narāḥ palitinas tathā āyuḥkṣayo manuṣyāṇāṃ kṣipram eva prapadyate
english: Men will grow grey at sixteen years of age, and the shortening of human life-span will come about very swiftly.

sanskrit: kṣīṇe yuge mahārāja taruṇā vṛddhaśīlinaḥ taruṇānāṃ ca yac chīlaṃ tad vṛddheṣu prajāyate
english: When the age is in decline, O great king, the young will have the ways of the old, and the conduct proper to the young will appear among the old.

sanskrit: viparītās tadā nāryo vañcayitvā rahaḥ patīn vyuccaranty api duḥśīlā dāsaiḥ paśubhir eva ca
english: Women, perverse in that time and of vile character, will secretly deceive their husbands and commit adultery even with slaves and animals.

sanskrit: tasmin yugasahasrānte saṃprāpte cāyuṣaḥ kṣaye anāvṛṣṭir mahārāja jāyate bahuvārṣikī
english: At the end of that thousand-year cycle, when the shortening of life has arrived, a drought lasting many years will arise, O great king.

sanskrit: tatas tāny alpasārāṇi sattvāni kṣudhitāni ca pralayaṃ yānti bhūyiṣṭhaṃ pṛthivyāṃ pṛthivīpate
english: Then those beings, who are of little substance and racked by hunger, will for the most part perish upon the earth, O guardian of the earth.

sanskrit: tato dinakarair dīptaiḥ saptabhir manujādhipa pīyate salilaṃ sarvaṃ samudreṣu saritsu ca
english: Then seven blazing suns will drink up all the water in the oceans and rivers, O lord of men.

sanskrit: yac ca kāṣṭhaṃ tṛṇaṃ cāpi śuṣkaṃ cārdraṃ ca bhārata sarvaṃ tad bhasmasād bhūtaṃ dṛśyate bharatarṣabha
english: Whatever is wood and whatever is grass, dry or wet, O Bhārata — all of it is seen reduced to ash, O bull of the Bhāratas.

sanskrit: tataḥ saṃvartako vahnir vāyunā saha bhārata lokam āviśate pūrvam ādityair upaśoṣitam
english: Then the fire of universal dissolution, together with the wind, O Bhārata, enters the world that was already parched by the suns.

sanskrit: tataḥ sa pṛthivīṃ bhittvā samāviśya rasātalam devadānavayakṣāṇāṃ bhayaṃ janayate mahat
english: Then, piercing the earth and penetrating into the netherworld, it generates great fear among the gods, demons, and yakṣas.

sanskrit: nirdahan nāgalokaṃ ca yac ca kiṃ cit kṣitāv iha adhastāt pṛthivīpāla sarvaṃ nāśayate kṣaṇāt
english: Burning the realm of the serpents and whatever else exists beneath the earth here, O guardian of the earth, it destroys everything in an instant.

sanskrit: tato yojanaviṃśānāṃ sahasrāṇi śatāni ca nirdahaty aśivo vāyuḥ sa ca saṃvartako 'nalaḥ
english: Then that inauspicious wind and that fire of dissolution together consume hundreds of thousands of twenty-yojana expanses.

sanskrit: sadevāsuragandharvaṃ sayakṣoragarākṣasam tato dahati dīptaḥ sa sarvam eva jagad vibhuḥ
english: Then that all-pervading, blazing fire burns the entire world together with gods, asuras, gandharvas, yakṣas, serpents, and rākṣasas.

sanskrit: tato gajakulaprakhyās taḍinmālāvibhūṣitāḥ uttiṣṭhanti mahāmeghā nabhasy adbhutadarśanāḥ
english: Then great clouds resembling herds of elephants, adorned with garlands of lightning, rise up in the sky, marvellous to behold.

sanskrit: ke cin nīlotpalaśyāmāḥ ke cit kumudasaṃnibhāḥ ke cit kiñjalkasaṃkāśāḥ ke cit pītāḥ payodharāḥ
english: Some are dark as blue lotuses, some resemble white water-lilies, some look like lotus filaments, and some are yellow cloud-masses.

sanskrit: ke cid dhāridrasaṃkāśāḥ kākāṇḍakanibhās tathā ke cit kamalapatrābhāḥ ke cid dhiṅgulakaprabhāḥ
english: Some are like turmeric in hue, some resemble the kākāṇḍaka fruit, some have the lustre of lotus petals, and some glow like asafoetida resin.

sanskrit: ke cit puravarākārāḥ ke cid gajakulopamāḥ ke cid añjanasaṃkāśāḥ ke cin makarasaṃsthitāḥ vidyunmālāpinaddhāṅgāḥ samuttiṣṭhanti vai ghanāḥ
english: Some are shaped like great cities, some resemble herds of elephants, some look like collyrium, some are formed like sea-monsters — their limbs wreathed with garlands of lightning, the clouds rise up in hosts.

sanskrit: ghorarūpā mahārāja ghorasvananināditāḥ tato jaladharāḥ sarve vyāpnuvanti nabhastalam
english: Terrible in form, O great king, resounding with dreadful thunder, all those rain-bearing clouds then pervade the expanse of the sky.

sanskrit: tair iyaṃ pṛthivī sarvā saparvatavanākarā āpūryate mahārāja salilaughapariplutā
english: By them this whole earth, with its mountains, forests, and mines, is filled to overflowing and flooded with torrents of water, O great king.

sanskrit: tatas te jaladā ghorā rāviṇaḥ puruṣarṣabha sarvataḥ plāvayanty āśu coditāḥ parameṣṭhinā
english: Then those fearsome roaring clouds, O bull among men, urged on by Brahmā, quickly inundate everything on all sides.

sanskrit: varṣamāṇā mahat toyaṃ pūrayanto vasuṃdharām sughoram aśivaṃ raudraṃ nāśayanti ca pāvakam
english: Pouring down mighty waters and filling the earth, they extinguish the most terrible, inauspicious, and fierce fire.

sanskrit: tato dvādaśa varṣāṇi payodās ta upaplave dhārābhiḥ pūrayanto vai codyamānā mahātmanā
english: Then for twelve years those clouds, in the great deluge, fill everything with their torrents, urged on by the great soul Brahmā.

sanskrit: tataḥ samudraḥ svāṃ velām atikrāmati bhārata parvatāś ca viśīryante mahī cāpi viśīryate
english: Then the ocean overflows its shoreline, O Bhārata, the mountains crumble, and the earth itself disintegrates.

sanskrit: sarvataḥ sahasā bhrāntās te payodā nabhastalam saṃveṣṭayitvā naśyanti vāyuvegaparāhatāḥ
english: Then those clouds, suddenly scattering in all directions, envelop the sky and vanish, struck down by the force of the wind.

sanskrit: tatas taṃ mārutaṃ ghoraṃ svayambhūr manujādhipa ādipadmālayo devaḥ pītvā svapiti bhārata
english: Then the self-born lord, O lord of men, that god whose primal abode is the lotus, drinks up that terrible wind and falls asleep, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: tasminn ekārṇave ghore naṣṭe sthāvarajaṅgame naṣṭe devāsuragaṇe yakṣarākṣasavarjite
english: In that terrible single ocean, when all that is moving and unmoving has perished, when the hosts of gods and asuras have perished, with yakṣas and rākṣasas gone —

sanskrit: nirmanuṣye mahīpāla niḥśvāpadamahīruhe anantarikṣe loke 'smin bhramāmy eko 'ham ādṛtaḥ
english: — with the earth empty of men, O guardian of the earth, devoid of beasts and great trees, with sky uninterrupted, in this world I alone wander with great care.

sanskrit: ekārṇave jale ghore vicaran pārthivottama apaśyan sarvabhūtāni vaiklavyam agamaṃ param
english: Wandering in the terrible water of that single ocean, O best of earthly lords, seeing no living beings at all, I fell into the utmost distress.

sanskrit: tataḥ sudīrghaṃ gatvā tu plavamāno narādhipa śrāntaḥ kva cin na śaraṇaṃ labhāmy aham atandritaḥ
english: Then, drifting for a very long time, O lord of men, I grew weary, and though tireless I found shelter nowhere.

sanskrit: tataḥ kadā cit paśyāmi tasmin salilasaṃplave nyagrodhaṃ sumahāntaṃ vai viśālaṃ pṛthivīpate
english: Then at a certain moment I beheld in that flood of waters a vast and expansive banyan tree, O guardian of the earth.

sanskrit: śākhāyāṃ tasya vṛkṣasya vistīrṇāyāṃ narādhipa paryaṅke pṛthivīpāla divyāstaraṇasaṃstṛte
english: On a wide branch of that tree, O lord of men, on a couch spread with a divine coverlet, O guardian of the earth —

sanskrit: upaviṣṭaṃ mahārāja pūrṇendusadṛśānanam phullapadmaviśālākṣaṃ bālaṃ paśyāmi bhārata
english: — I see a child seated there, O great king, whose face resembles the full moon, whose large eyes are like blooming lotuses, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: tato me pṛthivīpāla vismayaḥ sumahān abhūt kathaṃ tv ayaṃ śiśuḥ śete loke nāśam upāgate
english: Then a very great wonder arose in me, O guardian of the earth: how can this infant be resting when the world has come to its destruction?

sanskrit: tapasā cintayaṃś cāpi taṃ śiśuṃ nopalakṣaye bhūtaṃ bhavyaṃ bhaviṣyac ca jānann api narādhipa
english: Even concentrating my tapas and reflecting upon that infant, I could not discern him, though I know all that has been, all that is, and all that shall be, O lord of men.

sanskrit: atasīpuṣpavarṇābhaḥ śrīvatsakṛtalakṣaṇaḥ sākṣāl lakṣmyā ivāvāsaḥ sa tadā pratibhāti me
english: He was of the colour of a flax flower, marked with the Śrīvatsa sign — he appeared to me then as a dwelling-place of Śrī herself made manifest.

sanskrit: tato mām abravīd bālaḥ sa padmanibhalocanaḥ śrīvatsadhārī dyutimān vākyaṃ śrutisukhāvaham
english: Then that child, whose eyes resembled lotuses, who bore the Śrīvatsa mark and was radiant, spoke to me words pleasing to the ear.

sanskrit: jānāmi tvā pariśrāntaṃ tāta viśrāmakāṅkṣiṇam mārkaṇḍeya ihāssva tvaṃ yāvad icchasi bhārgava
english: 'I know you are weary and longing for rest, dear one. Sit here, Mārkaṇḍeya, as long as you wish, O descendant of Bhṛgu.'

sanskrit: abhyantaraṃ śarīraṃ me praviśya munisattama āssva bho vihito vāsaḥ prasādas te kṛto mayā
english: 'Enter within my body, O best of sages, and dwell there — a dwelling has been prepared for you; this grace is done to you by me.'

sanskrit: tato bālena tenaivam uktasyāsīt tadā mama nirvedo jīvite dīrghe manuṣyatve ca bhārata
english: Then, spoken to thus by that child, I felt at that moment a profound weariness with my long life and with the human condition, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: tato bālena tenāsyaṃ sahasā vivṛtaṃ kṛtam tasyāham avaśo vaktraṃ daivayogāt praveśitaḥ
english: Then that child suddenly opened his mouth, and I, helpless, was drawn by divine agency into that mouth.

sanskrit: tataḥ praviṣṭas tatkukṣiṃ sahasā manujādhipa sarāṣṭranagarākīrṇāṃ kṛtsnāṃ paśyāmi medinīm
english: Then, having entered that belly instantly, O lord of men, I see the entire earth crowded with kingdoms and cities.

sanskrit: gaṅgāṃ śatadruṃ sītāṃ ca yamunām atha kauśikīm carmaṇvatīṃ vetravatīṃ candrabhāgāṃ sarasvatīm
english: I see the Gaṅgā, the Śatadrū, the Sītā, the Yamunā, the Kauśikī, the Carmaṇvatī, the Vetravatī, the Candrabhāgā, and the Sarasvatī.

sanskrit: sindhuṃ caiva vipāśāṃ ca nadīṃ godāvarīm api vasvokasārāṃ nalinīṃ narmadāṃ caiva bhārata
english: And the Sindhu, the Vipāśā, the river Godāvarī, the Vasvokasārā, the Nalinī, and the Narmadā as well, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: nadīṃ tāmrāṃ ca veṇṇāṃ ca puṇyatoyāṃ śubhāvahām suveṇāṃ kṛṣṇaveṇāṃ ca irāmāṃ ca mahānadīm śoṇaṃ ca puruṣavyāghra viśalyāṃ kampunām api
english: The river Tāmrā, the Veṇṇā of holy and auspicious waters, the Suveṇā, the Kṛṣṇaveṇā, the Irāmā, the great river Śoṇa, O tiger among men, the Viśalyā, and the Kampu as well.

sanskrit: etāś cānyāś ca nadyo 'haṃ pṛthivyāṃ yā narottama parikrāman prapaśyāmi tasya kukṣau mahātmanaḥ
english: These and the other rivers of the earth, O best of men, I see as I wander through the belly of that great soul, beholding them as I roam.

sanskrit: tataḥ samudraṃ paśyāmi yādogaṇaniṣevitam ratnākaram amitraghna nidhānaṃ payaso mahat
english: Then I see the ocean, frequented by hosts of aquatic creatures, the mine of jewels, O slayer of foes, the great treasury of waters.

sanskrit: tataḥ paśyāmi gaganaṃ candrasūryavirājitam jājvalyamānaṃ tejobhiḥ pāvakārkasamaprabhaiḥ paśyāmi ca mahīṃ rājan kānanair upaśobhitām
english: Then I see the sky resplendent with moon and sun, blazing with radiances equal to fire and sun. And I see the earth, O king, adorned with forests.

sanskrit: yajante hi tadā rājan brāhmaṇā bahubhiḥ savaiḥ kṣatriyāś ca pravartante sarvavarṇānurañjane
english: For there brahmins perform sacrifice with abundant oblations, O king, and kṣatriyas apply themselves to the delighting of all the social orders.

sanskrit: vaiśyāḥ kṛṣiṃ yathānyāyaṃ kārayanti narādhipa śuśrūṣāyāṃ ca niratā dvijānāṃ vṛṣalās tathā
english: Vaiśyas carry on agriculture in the proper manner, O lord of men, and śūdras too are devoted to the service of the twice-born.
